composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"

# Validate required fields first, so a missing/blank field is a 400 listing every
# offending field before the body is mapped to an entity.
validate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkTelephoneUnique

# Reject with 409 when the normalized telephone is already used by another owner.
checkTelephoneUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkHouseholdUnique

# Reject with 409 when another owner shares this last name and address (compared
# case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace), unless the body sets 'sharesHousehold' true.
checkHouseholdUnique:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkCityCapacity

# Reject with 409 when the owner's city already contains 50 or more owners.
checkCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: checkDailyCreateLimit

# Reject with 429 when 100 or more owners have already been created today (by registrationDate).
checkDailyCreateLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.CheckOwnerDailyCreateLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# When the body set 'sharesHousehold' true, assign the new owner and the existing
# same-lastName/same-address owner(s) a single stable, shared 'householdId'.
assignHousehold:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdId
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignNamesakeCount

# Record how many existing owners share this owner's firstName and lastName
# (case-insensitively), before it is saved so the count excludes it.
assignNamesakeCount:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCode

# Assign the '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' customer code before saving, so the per-city
# owner count the sequence is derived from excludes this not-yet-persisted owner.
assignCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

save:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

# Emit an AUDIT log line carrying the owner id, customerCode and registrationDate,
# after save so the generated id is available.
audit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AuditOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

respond:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.RespondWithOwnerCreated
  govern: [ transaction ]

        lastName:

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin

          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'

          format: email

              type: string

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vets (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  first_name VARCHAR(30),
  last_name VARCHAR(30),
  INDEX(last_name)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS specialties (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(80),
  INDEX(name)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vet_specialties (
  vet_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  specialty_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  FOREIGN KEY (vet_id) REFERENCES vets(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (specialty_id) REFERENCES specialties(id),
  UNIQUE (vet_id,specialty_id)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS types (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(80),
  INDEX(name)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS owners (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  first_name VARCHAR(30),
  last_name VARCHAR(30),
  address VARCHAR(255),
  city VARCHAR(80),
  telephone VARCHAR(20),
  registration_date DATE,
  customer_code VARCHAR(30),
  household_id VARCHAR(64),
  namesake_count INT,
  INDEX(last_name)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pets (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  name VARCHAR(30),
  birth_date DATE,
  type_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  owner_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  INDEX(name),
  FOREIGN KEY (owner_id) REFERENCES owners(id),
  FOREIGN KEY (type_id) REFERENCES types(id)
) engine=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS visits (
  id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
  pet_id INT(4) UNSIGNED NOT NULL,
  visit_date DATE,
  description VARCHAR(255),
  FOREIGN KEY (pet_id) REFERENCES pets(id)
) engine=InnoDB;

  password VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL ,
  enabled TINYINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 ,
  PRIMARY KEY (username)
) engine=InnoDB;

Implemented the `bulkSignupWarning` field: **true when more than 80 owners were already created today, otherwise false**, following the same "created today" accumulation path as the existing daily-create-limit rule (owners whose adjusted business-day `registrationDate` equals today's business day).
